name: ComplemeNt Net Architecture
definition: CNNA is the throughgoing architecture in which one historically grown provenance net is repeatedly resolved into a realized or retained part, a cut- or stage-relative complement, and an interface through which effective response and the next birth are determined.
origin: The architecture begins with the transition from the empty carrier to the first realized node, becomes structurally explicit when the b-ary grammar distinguishes the born prefix from open continuation slots, and becomes a nontrivial response-capable net with the first non-root birth and its directed relation.
relative_complement_guard: Complement is relational and cut-, scale-, or projection-relative; it is not an intrinsic permanent partner assigned to each node.
proof_guard: No node receives additional mathematical force from this conceptual mapping.
